evals.name: do-i-need-to-run-a-worker
evals.prompt: I just finished setting up ConfigHub and I want to deploy a Kubernetes app to my cluster through ArgoCD. Do I need to run a worker process first?
evals.expected_output: Explains that OCI and ConfigHub delivery use server workers hosted in the ConfigHub server — no process to run. Creates one with cub worker create --space <s> --allow-exists --is-server-worker server-worker, and hands off to target-bind to create an OCI target against it. Notes ArgoCD is configured to pull from ConfigHub's OCI registry outside ConfigHub. Does not install or run an external worker.

evals.name: external-worker-for-custom-functions
evals.prompt: I've written some custom worker functions and want a worker that hosts them. How do I run that?
evals.expected_output: Explains that custom functions require an external worker (not a server worker): create the entity with cub worker create, then run it with cub worker run (local) or install it into a cluster with cub worker install --export | kubectl apply, and verify with cub worker list-function that the custom functions are advertised. Defers exact flags to cub worker run/install --help.

evals.name: diagnose-crashing-external-worker
evals.prompt: The external worker I installed yesterday for my custom functions is in CrashLoopBackOff. Help me figure out what's wrong.
evals.expected_output: Pulls cub worker status, cub worker logs, and kubectl describe pod for the worker pod; surfaces the specific error (image-pull, RBAC, missing secret, server-version mismatch, etc.); recommends a concrete next step — cub worker upgrade if version mismatch; fix RBAC / namespace permissions if authz; check the credential secret. Stops before retrying blindly.
